title: bug: in a project that commits .moe/tasks (the commitBoardState default), `git clean -fdx` deletes the runtime dirs without tripping the mass-deletion heal, so the reload empties workers, teams, proposals, leases and attempts
description:
Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/massDeletionHeal.ts and packages/moe-daemon/src/state/massDeletionHeal.test.ts. No open row declares either file. I checked the plan files of every non-DONE row at 2026-11-02 20:51Z. WT-16 owns commands/doctor.ts, which this row does not touch.

Defect, read at HEAD 3e092cff:
- healMassDeletion (massDeletionHeal.ts:25, :33-43) counts missing entities across tasks, epics, teams, workers and proposals together. It heals only when at least 3 are missing AND at least 20% of that combined total is missing.
- The heal was written for a fully gitignored .moe: px4swarm, 2026-09-25 and 09-26.
- Under settings.commitBoardState (default on), the wrappers commit .moe/tasks, .moe/epics and project.json. So in a board-tracking project, `git clean -fdx` (or `git stash --all`) deletes only the ignored or untracked runtime dirs:
  - workers/ and proposals/, ignored by .moe/.gitignore;
  - teams/, resources/, attempts/, candidates/, checks/, reviews/ and receipts/, ignored by this repo's root .gitignore:68-80.
- Example with this repo's live counts: 80 entities missing (13 workers + 6 teams + 61 proposals) out of 935 known. 80 is under 187 (20%), so the heal returns 0.
- The FileWatcher callback (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:805-813) then calls state.load(). load() replaces every map from disk (StateManager.ts:1078-1119), so workers, teams, proposals, resources, attempts, candidates, reviews, checkRuns and receipts all come back empty.
- Even when the heal does fire, it rewrites only those 5 kinds. The next reload then empties the runtime maps it never rewrote.

Consequences:
- Every assigned task's owner is missing from the worker map, so isTaskClaimable lets any idle seat claim a live seat's WORKING row.
- Held capacity-1 leases vanish, so the next acquire_resource is granted at once.
- Open attempts vanish, so the attempt generation restarts.
- Pending rail proposals are lost.

Reach: any project on the wrappers' default board commits, when a person or an agent runs `git clean -fdx` or `git stash --all` at the repo root while the daemon runs. That is exactly the trigger the heal exists for. A young board with few tasks still trips the combined 20% rule. A mature board never does.

Origin: hunt requested by governor-e6b40560 (msg-5fe3b1537cb04b50964bd0edf07db4c8). massDeletionHeal.ts has had one commit (ad4ff578). No row mentions its threshold or kinds.

Fix direction (exact rule decided at planning):
- Also detect a wipe per kind: a kind that loses at least MIN and at least FRACTION of its own entries, or whose whole directory is gone while memory still holds entries of it.
- Keep the combined rule.
- On a wipe, rewrite every entity map that load() replaces (add resources, attempts, candidates, reviews, checkRuns stored under checks/, receipts, channels and decisions).
- A deliberate deletion of one or two files must still reload.
definitionOfDone: New fixture: a store holding at least 50 tasks, 1 epic, 4 workers, 1 team, 3 proposals, one resource with a lease and one open attempt. The test deletes the workers/, teams/, proposals/, resources/ and attempts/ directories, then runs healMassDeletion followed by state.load(), the FileWatcher's order. Afterwards those maps hold exactly the entities they held before the deletion, and their files are back on disk.

Deleting a single worker file (and, separately, two proposal files) still makes healMassDeletion return 0, and the following load() drops exactly those entities, as today. The three existing cases in massDeletionHeal.test.ts pass unchanged.
RED first: the new wipe case fails against the unchanged massDeletionHeal.ts, and the completion evidence quotes the failure.

`cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/massDeletionHeal.test.ts src/state/StateManager.test.ts` exits 0. Run it in the task's worktree or in a git-archive snapshot, never as an in-place build or test in the shared control checkout. Its output is the complete_task evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX. Edit packages/moe-daemon/src/state/massDeletionHeal.ts only (DoD 5). Keep MASS_DELETION_MIN = 3 and MASS_DELETION_FRACTION = 0.2.

1. Replace KINDS with a STORES table: one [dir, (s: StateManager) => Map<string, unknown>] row for every map load() replaces (StateManager.ts about :1063-1119). The rows are tasks, epics, workers, teams, proposals, channels, decisions, resources, attempts, candidates, reviews, ['checks', s => s.checkRuns] and receipts. Use accessors, not string indexing, so `tsc --noEmit` checks every field.
2. One pass over STORES. For each store with entries:
   - dirGone = !fs.existsSync(join(moePath, dir));
   - an entity is missing when dirGone or its `<dir>/<id>.json` is absent (loadEntities keys by the entity's id field).
3. Keep the combined rule exactly as today: only over tasks, epics, teams, workers and proposals, missing >= MIN and >= FRACTION x their total.
4. Add the per-kind rule for every store EXCEPT tasks and epics: dirGone, or that kind's missing >= MIN and >= FRACTION x its own size.
   - tasks and epics are the board kinds the wrappers commit under settings.commitBoardState, so a git checkout or pull changes them on purpose.
5. On either rule, rewrite EVERY missing entity of EVERY store with state.writeEntity(dir, id, entity), then log the restored count per kind and which rule fired. Rewriting only some kinds would let the next load() empty the rest.
6. Otherwise return 0, so the caller reloads as before.

Update the header comment. It names the board-commit case (git clean -fdx / git stash --all delete only the ignored runtime dirs), states the two rules, and names the gaps:
- messages/ and pins/ are not in memory and cannot be restored;
- checks/dispatches and checks/observations load lazily (checkObservationStore) and are not replaced by load().

Re-run step 1's command with massDeletionHeal.ts copied in as well: every case passes.
implementationPlan.note: massDeletionHeal.ts: KINDS replaced by a STORES table of accessors for all 13 maps load() replaces (tasks, epics, workers, teams, proposals, channels, decisions, resources, attempts, candidates, reviews, checks→checkRuns, receipts). scanStores does one pass with one existsSync per entity plus one per dir; the combined rule keeps its arithmetic over tasks/epics/teams/workers/proposals only (isWipe = missing>=MIN && missing>=total*FRACTION, same as the old inverted check). The new per-kind rule covers every store except tasks/epics: dir gone while memory holds entries, or the kind lost >=3 and >=20% of its own. On either rule every missing entity of every store is rewritten via writeEntity, and the log names restoredByKind, the rule, and the wiped kinds. MIN/FRACTION values and exports unchanged. Header comment documents the board-commit case, both rules, and the gaps (messages/pins not in memory; checks/dispatches|observations lazy). GREEN in snapshot /tmp/tmp.cRFhb1ueFF: tsc --noEmit ok; massDeletionHeal.test.ts 7/7 pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: healMassDeletion also treats a per-kind runtime wipe as a wipe, and on any wipe rewrites every entity map load() replaces. A per-kind wipe is a non-board kind whose directory vanished while memory still holds entries, or that lost at least 3 and at least 20% of its own entries. So the `git clean -fdx` / `git stash --all` that removes only the ignored runtime dirs of a board-tracking project no longer lets the FileWatcher's reload empty workers, teams, proposals, leases or attempts. A deletion of one or two files still reloads as before.

A following load() restores all 5 maps deep-equal to before, with their files on disk.
(x) One worker file deleted, and (y) two proposal files deleted: the heal returns 0 and load() drops exactly those entities. The 3 existing cases pass unchanged.
RED: (w) fails against the unchanged heal, and the completion summary quotes it.
invariants: MASS_DELETION_MIN and MASS_DELETION_FRACTION keep their values and exports; the combined rule's kinds and arithmetic are unchanged.
tasks and epics never trip the per-kind rule.
Only massDeletionHeal.ts and its test change (DoD 5); index.ts's caller is untouched.
No npm in the shared checkout.

state/persistence.ts loadEntities keys each map by the entity's id and tolerates a missing dir; writeEntity(kind, id, entity) writes <moePath>/<kind>/<id>.json and mkdirs.
packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts FileWatcher callback: `if ((await healMassDeletion(state)) > 0) return; await state.load();`.
This repo commits .moe/tasks, epics and channels, and ignores workers/, proposals/ (.moe/.gitignore) and teams/, resources/, attempts/, candidates/, checks/, reviews/, receipts/ (root .gitignore).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Running the per-kind rule over tasks and epics too was rejected. They are committed under commitBoardState, so a branch switch that drops 20% of task files would be resurrected instead of reloaded, a behavior change for git-tracked boards. Widening the combined denominator to all 13 kinds was rejected: it would make the existing combined rule less sensitive. Healing in index.ts was rejected too, because DoD 5 limits the change to the two files.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- load() backfills (worker.teamId null and task priority/comments), so fixture entities created through the APIs round-trip deep-equal.
- ensureChatInfrastructure recreates canonical channels with NEW ids when channels/ is missing. Healing channels keeps message files keyed to the old channel ids.
- In this repo channels/ is committed, but other projects may ignore it.
planningNotes.risks:
- messages/ (chat history) and pins/ are deleted by the same git clean, but they are not in memory, so they are out of scope.
- checks/dispatches and observations are lazy WeakMap stores not replaced by load(); their files stay lost until the next write. Note it in the header comment.
- A deliberate bulk hand-deletion of at least 20% (at least 3) of a runtime kind is now undone. That is acceptable: .moe/ is never edited by hand.
